signals.title: USD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Hawkish Rates
signals.text: The G10 currency scorecard shows USD outperforming the board at +1.141% across 9 pairs while NOK lags at -1.794% across 2 pairs, generating a 2.935% spread. Hawkish remarks from Chicago Fed President Goolsbee emphasizing elevated inflation reinforce the policy disparity, while US 5Y yields rose +23bp over 5 sessions led entirely by real yields (+22bp). USD/NOK spot trades at 9.765, positioned firmly above its SMA20 at 9.430, SMA50 at 9.458, and SMA200 at 9.489. Although the Fed at 4.00% maintains a 50bp policy rate deficit against Norges Bank at 4.50%, persistent equity weakness and broad dollar demand keep upward pressure intact. The pair is extended well above short-term moving averages, pointing to trend continuation despite the nominal carry headwind. Trade bias: Bullish USD/NOK, sustained by broad dollar dominance across G10. Catalyst: Fed Governor Waller speech on 20 Nov. Risk: Norges Bank hawkish pushback or crude oil rebound driving a sharp mean-reversion move toward the 9.489 SMA200 anchor.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Safe-Haven Divergence + Geopolitical Strain
signals.text: USD/JPY holds at 159.66, remaining just below the 160.00 watch level where past verbal warnings and intervention scrutiny emerged. The pair trades above its SMA20 (158.53), SMA50 (157.85), and SMA200 (158.83) cluster. A 269bp OIS carry premium (SOFR 3.92% vs TONA 1.23%) anchors structural upside, but elevated equity stress reflected in VIX at 28.4 alongside mounting Strait of Hormuz geopolitical risks introduces acute safe-haven friction. The rolling 252-day correlation between USD/JPY and VIX sits at +0.010 against a historical norm of +0.282 (z = -2.02σ), signaling a notable decoupling from conventional equity-risk relationships. The 25-delta risk reversal at -1.41 shows an active put skew as participants hedge spot downside against policy response risk. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY, balancing 269bp carry support against intervention risk at 160.00. Catalyst: Japan National CPI release on 19 Nov at 23:30 UTC. Risk: Spot break above 160.00 prompting direct MoF/BoJ intervention action.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short + Policy Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.0971, marking a 0.72% 1W decline and holding entirely below its falling SMA20 (1.1127), SMA50 (1.1246), and SMA200 (1.1509) in a confirmed technical downtrend. CFTC Leveraged Funds maintain an extended net short of -98,604 contracts, placing positioning at the 6th percentile of its 52-week range (z = -1.58). The fundamental backdrop remains defined by a 135bp policy rate gap favoring the Fed at 4.00% over the ECB at 2.65%, reinforced by an OIS spread of +148bp (SOFR 3.92% vs €STR 2.44%). Front-month options pricing shows ATM IV at 6.0% against HV30 at 5.0%, establishing a +1.0% volatility risk premium as downside demand holds. With speculative shorts near multi-month extremes, the downtrend remains intact but vulnerable to sharp positioning squeezes on positive domestic news. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, supported by 148bp OIS carry advantage for the dollar. Catalyst: ECB President Lagarde speech on 20 Nov at 08:30 UTC. Risk: A daily close above the 1.1127 SMA20 triggering Leveraged Funds short covering.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning + Volatility + Retail
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6661, down 2.14% on the week following a 43,500 contraction in Australian employment. The pair sits below its SMA20 (0.6904), SMA50 (0.6975), and SMA200 (0.7048) cluster, extended 5.09 ATR below its 20-day average. CFTC data shows institutional Leveraged Funds net long +41,195 contracts (pctl 40, z +0.05), while retail positioning on Retail sentiment data displays an extreme 87% long stance. Options pricing reveals an inverted volatility risk premium, with 1M ATM IV at 7.7% running below HV30 at 8.3% (VRP -0.6%), reflecting subdued options premium despite severe spot spot losses. The RBA's 4.85% policy rate maintains an 85bp carry advantage over the Fed's 4.00%, but softening domestic economic data and cross-asset risk-off flows dominate the tape. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD, driven by labor market weakness overriding nominal carry support. Catalyst: Australia CFTC positioning update on 20 Nov at 20:30 UTC. Risk: Rebound back above the 0.6904 SMA20 invalidating the immediate breakdown.
